assessment: In this manuscript, the authors report that a major component of the pancreatic cancer microenvironment, hyaluronic acid, provides an important source of metabolic intermediates required for pancreatic cancer growth during conditions of nutrient limitation. Overall, this work nicely combines multiple cell lines and genetic approaches to show that scavenging of N-acetyl-glucosamine from hyaluronic acid supports cancer cell growth when de novo synthesis of N-acetyl-glucosamine is limited. More broadly, this work highlights how reliance on certain metabolic enzymes can vary depending on whether cells are grown in vitro or in vivo and provides evidence that environmental nutrient scavenging can contribute to differential metabolic dependencies of cancer cells.
